issues.legal_issue: An arbitral award that specifically allots immovable partnership assets creates rights in that property and requires registration, unlike an assignment of a partner’s share in the partnership.
material_facts: The award expressly allotted the factory and the partnership’s other assets and properties exclusively to one partner and made him absolutely entitled to them.
The parties accepted that the award dealt with immovable property worth more than the applicable registration threshold.
The allotment was made in return for payments and other reciprocal obligations; the award did not expressly or by necessary implication merely assign one partner’s share in the partnership.
issues.conclusion: The award created rights in immovable property and required registration; because it was unregistered, it was inadmissible for the purpose of pronouncing judgment in accordance with it.
issues.legal_principle: Under section 17 of the Registration Act, an instrument creating rights in immovable property of the relevant value requires registration. A partner’s share in partnership assets, even where those assets include immovable property, is movable property, and assignment of that share does not itself require registration: Ajudhia Parshad Ram Parshad v. Sham Sunder, Addanki Narayanappa v. Bhaskara Krishtappa, and Commissioner of Income-tax v. Juggilal Kamalapat. The Court applied Satish Kumar v. Surinder Kumar in holding that an award creating rights in immovable property requires registration.

rule.if: arbitration_award_present and court_asked_to_enter_judgment and award_allots_specific_immovable_assets and property_value_exceeds_registration_threshold and award_does_not_merely_assign_partner_share and award_is_unregistered

predicates.arbitration_award_present: The parties referred their dispute to arbitrators, who made an award.
predicates.court_asked_to_enter_judgment: A party asked a court to pronounce judgment in accordance with the award.
predicates.award_allots_specific_immovable_assets: The award expressly allotted identified immovable assets to a party and made that party entitled to them.
predicates.property_value_exceeds_registration_thre: The immovable property dealt with by the award was worth more than the value at which registration is required.
predicates.award_does_not_merely_assign_partner_sha: The award allotted specific partnership assets rather than merely assigning one partner’s interest in the partnership.
predicates.award_is_unregistered: The award had not been registered.

issues.definition: When a party seeks judgment on an award that specifically allots valuable immovable assets rather than merely assigning a partnership share, an unregistered award cannot be used for that judgment.

issues.legal_issue: A court cannot pronounce judgment under the arbitration procedure on an unregistered award that requires registration and is therefore inadmissible.
material_facts: The award created rights in immovable property and was unregistered.
The respondent’s application to set aside the award was dismissed as time-barred, after which the appellant asked the court to pronounce judgment in accordance with the award.
issues.conclusion: The court could not look into the unregistered award and could not pronounce judgment in accordance with it; dismissal of the challenge as time-barred did not make the award admissible.
issues.legal_principle: Section 17 of the Arbitration Act, 1940 presupposes an award that the court may validly look into. An award inadmissible for want of registration cannot support judgment under that section. The registration requirement follows from section 17 of the Registration Act and the rule applied in Satish Kumar v. Surinder Kumar.

predicates.court_asked_to_enter_judgment: A party asked a court to pronounce judgment in accordance with an arbitral award.
predicates.award_requires_registration: The award created rights in immovable property of a kind and value that require registration.
predicates.award_is_unregistered: The award had not been registered.

issues.definition: If a court is asked to enter judgment on an award that requires registration but was not registered, the court cannot pronounce judgment on that award.

issues.legal_issue: An inseparable unregistered arbitral award cannot be enforced in part by severing provisions that do not themselves deal with immovable property.
material_facts: The award combined the allotment of the factory and other assets with payment obligations, allocation of debts, waivers, assistance with recovery and transfer of tenancy rights, and delivery of business documents.
The award conditioned running the factory on payment of the consideration to the other partner.
The award was unregistered and its provisions formed an integrated arrangement in which the other clauses constituted consideration for the property allotment.
issues.conclusion: The award was an inseparable tangle of clauses and could not be enforced as to the parts that did not deal with immovable property.
issues.legal_principle: Section 17 of the Arbitration Act, 1940 applies only to an award that may validly be looked into by the court. Because this award was unregistered and its clauses were interdependent, the court could not enforce selected portions while excluding the provisions creating rights in immovable property.

predicates.court_asked_to_enforce_part_of_award: A party asked the court to give effect to only part of an arbitral award.
predicates.award_is_unregistered: The award had not been registered.
predicates.award_clauses_are_interdependent: The award linked its property allotment to other obligations, and those obligations formed consideration for the allotment.

issues.definition: When a party seeks to enforce only part of an unregistered award whose provisions are interdependent, the award cannot be enforced in part.
